spatial_claims.claim: A and B are endpoints of the chord bounding the segment, lying on the circumference of circle Gamma
C is a point on the circular arc of the segment, on the circumference of Gamma
A, B, C are not collinear (if collinear, the middle point would be inside Gamma by 3.2, contradicting being on circumference)
M is the midpoint of segment AB, lying on AB
N is the midpoint of segment AC, lying on AC
Line l is perpendicular to AB at M
Line m is perpendicular to AC at N
Center O lies on line l (case 1: if O on AB then O=M; case 2: if O not on AB then OM perpendicular to AB at M by 3.3, so OM coincides with l)
Center O lies on line m (same argument applied to chord AC)
M and N are distinct points (otherwise A, B, C would be collinear)
Lines l and m are distinct (if coincident, AB and AC would be parallel by 1.28, but they meet at A)
Intersection point X of l and m equals O (unique intersection of two distinct lines both containing O)
Circle with center X=O and radius XA has the same center and radius as Gamma

configuration_map: Points A, B lie on the circumference of circle Gamma as endpoints of the bounding chord of the segment. Point C lies on the arc of the segment, also on the circumference. M is the midpoint of AB (on the segment AB), N is the midpoint of AC (on the segment AC). Line l passes through M perpendicular to AB; line m passes through N perpendicular to AC. The center O of Gamma is shown to lie on both l and m. Since l and m are distinct (proven via 1.28 and the non-collinearity of A, B, C), their unique intersection X equals O. Throughout the proof, M stays on AB, N stays on AC, O stays on both l and m, and no point changes its relative position.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof uses perpendicular bisectors of chords AB and AC to locate the center, which is a standard geometrically valid construction. The case analysis for O on vs. off chord AB is correct, the distinctness of the perpendicular bisectors is properly justified via 1.28 and non-collinearity, and no angle decomposition or interior/exterior point arguments are employed. There are no contradictory spatial assumptions between any pair of steps.
